piece.caption: How to connect ChatGPT to Google Sheets CRM and Google Docs using Zapier MCP. If you spend time manually copying ChatGPT summaries into Google Docs, sheets, or CRM tools, connecting Zapier MCP changes the workflow. You connect your apps once in Zapier, and ChatGPT can create records or update rows directly inside the chat window. Zapier manages your app credentials, meaning AI models never touch your login keys. You can also restrict actions so the AI can create drafts but cannot delete records or send unauthorized messages. What daily copy-paste task between ChatGPT and your business apps takes up most of your time? Comment MCP for the step-by-step setup guide.

piece.dm_text: Zapier MCP Setup Steps for ChatGPT and Claude: 1. Open Zapier MCP dashboard and click +New MCP Server. Select ChatGPT or Claude as client. 2. Click +Add tool, search for your app (like Google Sheets, Docs, or CRM), and click its tile. 3. Select the exact action events allowed, then click Connect. 4. Click kebab menu (⋮) -> Configure to set fields, then click Save. 5. Click Connect at top of MCP dashboard to link server to your AI account. Zapier handles app logins so your keys remain safe. Full guide: https://zapier.com/blog/automate-chatgpt-zapier-mcp

[66] Zapier Blog — 4 ways to automate ChatGPT with Zapier MCP
URL: https://zapier.com/blog/automate-chatgpt-zapier-mcp
Lots of AI tools give you ways to take action in other apps, and I've tried a handful of them. The problem is they're almost always locked to one ecosystem, or they connect to just one app at a time, which defeats the purpose. I'd get something working, then hit a wall the moment I needed it to reach into a different corner of my stack.
Zapier MCP is different. Install it once in ChatGPT (or any AI tool that supports MCP) and it can reach 10,000+ apps, with Zapier handling each app's login so ChatGPT never touches your keys. That means ChatGPT can create records, update rows, and send messages across your stack without you ever leaving the chat window.
And when something needs to happen again and again, ChatGPT can build it as a Zap, an automated workflow that Zapier keeps running after you close the tab. Below, I'm sharing four workflows with templates to help you get started quickly with Zapier in ChatGPT.
Pro tip: Not sure which ChatGPT model to use for your workflows? Our guide to AI models on Zapier covers every model available from Anthropic, OpenAI, and other providers.
Draft and save long-form content to Google Docs
Research a prospect and update their HubSpot record
Summarize a meeting and send follow-up tasks in Asana
Pull data from a Google Sheet and write a weekly report to Notion
Before you try these workflows, you'll need to install Zapier MCP into ChatGPT if you haven't already. If you can click, type, and copy-paste, you can set this up in minutes. Just follow these steps:
Click +New MCP Server and choose ChatGPT as the client.
Now set up your first action. Click +Add tool.
Search for the app you want to connect to, then click its corresponding tile.
Select whichever action events you want to connect, then click Connect.
In the dashboard, configure each action according to your needs by clicking the kebab menu ( ⋮ ) and then Configure and adjusting values as needed. Hover over the tooltip icons next to any field for more details. When you're done, click Save.
Finally, click Connect at the top of the MCP dashboard and follow the instructions to add this server to your ChatGPT account.
Now you're ready to try the workflows below in ChatGPT.
Draft and save long-form content to Google Docs
You're a content marketer or writer who needs to produce first drafts fast—and you don't want to spend the next twenty minutes reformatting text and moving it into a doc. With ChatGPT connected to Google Docs via Zapier, the draft lands where it belongs.
Read a content brief, write a blog post draft, and save it to Google Docs automatically
Research a prospect and update their HubSpot record
You're in sales or RevOps, and you want ChatGPT to do the pre-call research you never have time for—and actually write the findings back to HubSpot so they're there when you need them.
Search for recent company news and add a research summary to their HubSpot record before your call
Summarize a meeting and send follow-up tasks in Asana
You're a project manager or team lead who wants ChatGPT to turn raw meeting notes into a clean summary and assigned tasks—so nothing gets lost after the call ends.
Turn meeting notes into a summary and assigned tasks in Asana automatically
Pull data from a Google Sheet and write a report to Notion
You're an analyst or ops lead who tracks metrics in a spreadsheet and wants a narrative summary written and filed automatically.
Analyze spreadsheet metrics, write an executive summary, and save it to Notion automatically
Every workflow above starts when you ask, but for some of them, you'll want it to work without having to ask. The weekly Sheets-to-Notion report is the obvious one. After you've run it a couple of times, tell ChatGPT: "Every Monday at 8 a.m., pull last week's numbers from the Metrics sheet, write a short summary, and save it to our Notion reports page." ChatGPT drafts the Zap and deploys it to Zapier. Automations like this can start on a schedule or when something happens in your apps, instead of waiting for you to open a chat.
A few things keep it dependable over time:
Same result every time. AI handles the part that needs judgment, like writing the summary. Pulling the rows and filing the page are regular steps, so Monday's report comes out just like Friday's.
Fixes what breaks. If someone renames the sheet or a login expires, the run shows up as failed in your logs, and Zapier finds the problem and proposes a fix. You can approve it or work through it with ChatGPT.
Cheaper and sturdier over time. If an AI step ends up doing the same thing on every run, Zapier can offer to swap it for a regular step: same result, fewer tokens.
These four workflows are just a starting point. Once ChatGPT has live access to your tools, you can string together almost any sequence of research, decision, and action—without leaving the conversation or writing a line of code. ChatGPT's built-in connectors cover the basics, like looking up a record or updating a field. Zapier goes further, so ChatGPT can do things like enroll a contact in a HubSpot nurture sequence or create an Asana task with an owner and a due date. And because your connections live in Zapier, they follow you: they work from Claude, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Cursor, or any other AI tool that supports MCP, so switching tools doesn't mean starting over.
If you want to go deeper, the Zapier MCP feature guide walks you through connecting your apps to ChatGPT step by step, with more detail on configuration, permissions, and what to try next.
Why use Zapier if I already have ChatGPT?
Keep ChatGPT—Zapier gives it more to work with. ChatGPT's built-in connectors cover a handful of popular apps, while Zapier reaches 10,000+ apps and keeps your Zaps running once the chat is closed. If one breaks, Zapier finds the problem and proposes the fix.
Partly. A scheduled task wakes up at a set time and has the model redo every step from scratch, which is slower and uses more tokens. A Zap can run on a schedule too, but it can also start the moment something happens, like a new row, ticket, or email, and it brings in AI only for the steps that need it. That makes it quicker to run, cheaper, and more consistent.
You can, and it will probably work the first time. The catch is everything after: a script needs somewhere to run, a way to catch events, and someone watching it. When an API changes or a login expires, it stops quietly, and it's usually storing your keys on a laptop or in a repo. If ChatGPT builds a Zap instead, Zapier hosts it, runs it on real triggers, and manages the connections. When something breaks, you get a proposed fix to approve.

[68] Zapier Blog — How to automate Claude safely with Zapier MCP
URL: https://zapier.com/blog/automate-claude-zapier-mcp
I've been playing this game at coffee shops where every time I overhear somebody say they're "building with AI," I take a sip of my cold brew. Suffice it to say, I'm staying caffeinated (and staying up at night).
Your IT admins may be losing sleep too, if everyone's handing AI tools like Claude access to their work apps, giving it more chances to do something it shouldn't. Zapier MCP closes that gap, connecting Claude to your tech stack with governance built in. That way, your AI can take only the actions you allow.
Below, I'll show you how to install Zapier MCP in Claude—whether you prefer to work in Chat or Code—and share a few templates to get you started fast. I'll also show you how Claude can turn repeat work into an automation that Zapier runs for you, starting whenever something happens in your apps. Claude does the building, and Zapier keeps it running.
Note: The templates in this post work with any AI tool that supports MCP, not just Claude.
Should I use Zapier MCP with Claude Chat or Claude Code?
5 ways to automate Claude with Zapier MCP
Zapier MCP is a tool you install in your AI to connect it to your other apps. It's for when you want to go beyond prompting and have AI carry out work for you. For example, instead of just asking Claude to write you an email that you'll send to your vendor list, maybe you want it to reach into your CRM, pull the names and addresses for a group of vendors, and create a draft in Gmail without navigating away from your Claude window. That's the kind of thing Zapier MCP makes possible.
AI tools come with native connectors of their own. But Zapier MCP is different because you decide exactly what Claude can do. You install it once with a few clicks, then give it access to just the apps and actions you allow. If you want Claude to draft a reply but never to send one, setting that up is easy. So is making sure it can never delete any records in your apps. And you can revoke access to an app or action anytime your needs change.
Claude's built-in connectors cover the basics, like looking up a record or updating a field. Zapier goes deeper, so Claude can do things like convert a lead in Salesforce or enroll a contact in a HubSpot nurture sequence, across 10,000+ apps. You connect your accounts once, and the same connections work from Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or any other AI tool that supports MCP, so switching tools doesn't mean starting over.
I've heard people claim that AI won't do anything you don't want it to, as long as you give it the right instructions. That reminds me of a favorite phrase of my brother-in-law: "I pretty much guarantee it." When everyone at your company is tinkering with AI, you need more than a "pretty-much guarantee" that it won't leak credentials or take some other improper action. You need the security Zapier MCP provides.
Should I use Zapier MCP with Claude Chat or Claude Code?
Once you've decided Claude should act on your apps within limits you set, the next question is where to install Zapier MCP. If you're working in Claude, your options are Claude Chat, Claude Code, or some mix of the two.
To help you decide, here's a rundown of what Zapier MCP unlocks in each.
Pro tip: Not sure which Claude model to use for your workflows? Our guide to AI models on Zapier covers every model available from Anthropic, OpenAI, and other providers.
Chat is the surface most people mean when they just say "Claude." It's a chat interface, but it can also work with the files on your computer, use your apps, and run code (this part used to be called Claude Cowork). It can even control your screen directly by clicking, typing, and navigating on its own. Plus, it lets you build tasks that run on a schedule.
With Zapier MCP installed, you can request one-off actions in your other apps without ever leaving your Claude conversation. This means you can build more complex workflows while retaining control over exactly which apps and actions Claude can touch.
Note: Claude can run scheduled tasks, but only while your computer is on and the desktop app is open. Once you close the app, the session stops. These are time-based automations, too, not event-based ones. If you want a workflow to run whether your computer is open or not, or to fire from an event-based trigger, build a Zap instead, and ask Claude to draft it for you through Zapier MCP. A Zap can start when something happens in an app or on a schedule, so it keeps working with your laptop closed. You can still use AI in a Zap workflow: add AI steps from your preferred model with our built-in tool, AI by Zapier , and let regular steps handle the rest.
Claude Code is an AI coding assistant. It's built to understand and act on a codebase specifically—tracing logic across files, working directly with git, running tests, and opening pull requests. It works wherever you write software, whether that's the terminal, your IDE, the desktop app, or your phone.
Install Zapier MCP into Claude Code, and you get conversational access to your apps right alongside your code. So you can say "post this to Slack" or "grab my open Jira tickets" mid-task without switching tools. And as with Chat, you can build time-based automations.
Claude Code also comes with another option: You can install the Zapier SDK here instead of Zapier MCP. The SDK is a set of building blocks for wiring Zapier's actions straight into your code, so when you need loops, error handling, multi-app chains, or something that runs autonomously in the background, you've got full programmatic control.
So which do you pick? It comes down to what you're making. Using Zapier MCP with Claude Code is best when the action is the end goal: you want something done right now, inside the conversation, and then you move on. The SDK is best when the code is the end goal, when you're building something that outlives the conversation, runs on its own schedule, and can be refined over time.
Before you try the workflows below, you'll need to install Zapier MCP into Claude if you haven't already. If you can click, type, and copy-paste, you can set this up in minutes. Just follow these steps:
Click +New MCP Server and choose Claude or Claude Code as the client.
Now set up your first action. Click +Add tool .
Search for the app you want to connect to, then click its corresponding tile .
Select whichever action events you want to connect, then click Connect .
In the dashboard, configure each action according to your needs by clicking the kebab menu (⋮) and then Configure and adjusting values as needed. Hover over the tooltip icons next to any field for more details. When you're done, click Save .
Finally, click Connect at the top of the MCP dashboard and follow the instructions to add this server to your Claude account.
